title: All-India Muslim League Founded in Dhaka
subtitle: A major organizational turning point in Muslim politics of British India.
summary: In December 1906, the All-India Muslim League was founded at Dhaka during the Muhammadan Educational Conference. The formation of the League created a new all-India political platform that sought Muslim representation within colonial constitutional politics and would later play a central role in partition-era negotiations.
heroTagline: Dhaka emerged as a symbolic site in the reorganization of all-India Muslim politics.
whyItMatters: The 1906 founding linked Bengal's political space to broader subcontinental constitutional debates, shaping later questions of representation, communal politics, and state formation.
